result.title: DR-LiteNet: A Lightweight Explainable Hybrid CNN Framework for Imbalanced Diabetic Retinopathy Grading via Adaptive SMOTE Fusion
result.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Accepted at the 1st International Conference on Next-Generation Electrical & Electronics, Computer Systems, and Technologies (iCONEECT)
result.summary: Automated diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading from colour fundus photographs is held back by two compounding challenges: severe class imbalance across five severity grades and the heavy computational cost of large scale architectures in resource constrained clinical settings. We introduce DR-LiteNet, a dual branch hybrid convolutional neural network that tackles both problems at once. The CNN branch extracts 1,280 dimensional deep features through EfficientNetB0, while the handcrafted (HC) branch produces a compact 51 dimensional lesion descriptor capturing vessel density, exudate intensity, texture entropy, and HSV colour histograms. Concatenating both branches yields a 1,331-d hybrid embedding, on which Adaptive SMOTE (ADASYN) is applied during training to synthesise minority class feature vectors, correcting distributional skew without touching the image space. A two phase training protocol first warms up the classification head on balanced features, then fine tunes the full network end to end. Grad CAM saliency maps deliver post-hoc clinical explainability. Tested on APTOS 2019 under five fold stratified cross validation, DR-LiteNet reaches 88.77% +/- 0.61 accuracy, a quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) of 0.884 +/- 0.010, and a macro F1 of 0.792 +/- 0.008 with only 4.69 M parameters beating ResNet50 (23.5 M) by DeltaQWK = 0.022 while staying practical on a single Google Colab T4 GPU. The source code of this project is available at: https://github.com/Nishi-Kanta-Paul/DR-LiteNet.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DR-LiteNet，一个双分支轻量 CNN 框架，用 EfficientNetB0 深度特征与 51 维手工病灶描述子拼接，并在特征空间用 ADASYN 合成少数类以缓解五级糖尿病视网膜病变分级中的类别不平衡，辅以两阶段训练和 Grad-CAM 解释。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于特定医学影像分级任务的分辨率与不平衡工程优化，不涉及 latent 推理状态、证据获取或停止决策，也未提供可变计算或状态抽象方面的可核查线索，故排除。
